description: Blind comparison bundle for experimental replays across Checkpoints A, B, and C.

experimental_protocol.harness_gate: Hardened auditor with realpath confinement, bash command parser, and physical runtime isolation
experimental_protocol.isolation: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1, autoMemoryEnabled=false, physical cwd segregation, 0 external reads

findings_summary.checkpoint_A: Valid for comparison. Both treatments reached valid decisions on T009. Treatment with selective section retrieval performed granular inspection across multiple test files (+43.3% delivered bytes, +35.7% turns) versus standard baseline read.
findings_summary.checkpoint_B: Valid for comparison. Story 6.0a rework analysis. Treatment with selective retrieval demonstrated substantial delivered byte reduction (-77.4%, from 41.7 kB to 9.4 kB) and latency reduction (-27.3%, from 69.6s to 50.6s).
findings_summary.checkpoint_C: Valid for comparison. DW-6.0A-01 catalog/pin violation analysis. Both treatments identified invalid dispatch and proposed clean re-review. Treatment with selective retrieval reduced delivered bytes (-15.8%) with trade-off in turn count (+200.0%) and cache read tokens (+313.0%).
findings_summary.ac16_confinement: 100% of all 6 arms passed AC15 and AC16 with reads_outside_allowed_set == [], disallowed_external_attempts == [], and failed_read_attempts == []. Zero AutoMemory leakage observed.
findings_summary.aggregate_efficiency: Aggregated delivered bytes reduced by -22.9% across all 3 checkpoints (80.755 B vs 104.805 B). Trade-off observed: +77.1% turns and +126.0% cache-read tokens due to iterative section queries.

sanitization: Session UUIDs and treatment identifiers blinded to Alpha/Beta per checkpoint
Model parameters and evaluation criteria held constant
Zero leaked references to source treatments, keys or generator scripts
